records.title: Coolant / water pump leak on TFSI engines (cracked plastic pump housing)
records.description: Q2 petrol owners report coolant loss from a leaking water pump at relatively low mileage — one documented 2018 Q2 case at only ~30,000 miles. The EA888/EA211 TFSI family uses an integrated plastic water-pump/thermostat housing that becomes brittle and cracks (commonly at the plastic pipe ports or the shaft seal behind the drive gear), causing seepage or sudden coolant loss. A failing pump bearing can also misalign the pulley. Left unchecked, coolant loss leads to overheating; on belt-driven engines a degraded pump can also threaten timing-belt integrity.
records.solution: Replace the water pump and thermostat housing (typically an updated revised unit) and refill/bleed with the correct G13 coolant; many shops do this together with the timing belt service. Inspect related coolant hoses/thermostat at the same time.
symptoms: Low coolant warning / repeatedly topping up coolant
Coolant smell or visible pink/orange residue at front of engine

records.title: Diesel particulate filter (DPF) clogging on TDI engines used for short trips
records.description: Q2 TDI diesels (1.6 TDI / 2.0 TDI) suffer from DPF clogging when the car is mostly used for short, low-speed urban journeys. The soot filter never reaches the exhaust temperature needed to complete a passive/active regeneration, so soot accumulates, the DPF warning light comes on, and the car may enter a forced-regen cycle or limp mode. Repeated interrupted regens (driver slowing/stopping before the cycle finishes) make it worse and can dilute engine oil with diesel.
records.solution: Drive at a steady speed (>60 km/h / ~40 mph) under moderate load for 15–30 minutes to allow regeneration to complete; if blocked, the dealer performs a forced/static regeneration with diagnostic equipment. Severely blocked filters need professional DPF cleaning or replacement. Long-term: avoid exclusively short trips.

records.title: Electro-mechanical parking brake can release on its own (recall 45H4)
records.description: An official safety recall covers Q2s built 1 Jan 2017 – 30 Jun 2018 in which the electro-mechanical (electronic) parking brake may be inadvertently released while the clutch pedal is being released. On a manual-transmission car parked on an incline this creates a vehicle roll-away hazard. The cause is a fault in the parking-brake control software. Around 3,650 UK vehicles were affected.
records.solution: Recall remedy (Audi reference 45H4): the parking-brake control unit software is reprogrammed/updated at an authorised Audi dealer free of charge. As a workaround until done, owners are advised to leave the car in gear when parked on a slope.
symptoms: Parking brake disengages unexpectedly when clutch released

records.title: Fuse-carrier power connector recall — engine, instrument cluster or lights can fail (RHD A3/Q2)
records.description: An official recall covers right-hand-drive Audi Q2 (and A3) vehicles built 2019–2023 in which the plug connector on the supply line for the interior fuse carrier may not have been installed correctly. Over time the connection can work loose, cutting power to multiple electrical functions. The consequence is failure of the engine, the instrument cluster display, or the lighting — and if it occurs while driving, the engine can switch off, creating a stalling/crash risk. The campaign affected roughly 137,573 vehicles (UK figure ~104,000+).
records.solution: Recall remedy (Audi code 97HO; KBA reference 013099): an authorised Audi workshop inspects and correctly secures/replaces the fuse-box plug connection free of charge. Owners check eligibility via VIN at an Audi dealer.
symptoms: Engine cuts out / stalls while driving

records.title: MMI infotainment freezing/rebooting and intermittent electrical glitches
records.description: Owner reliability surveys for the Q2 repeatedly flag faulty infotainment and minor electrical issues as the most common complaint type. The MMI screen can freeze, go black and reboot itself (sometimes while driving), and dashboard warning lights appear with no obvious cause. Causes are usually software bugs, corrupt phone-pairing/Bluetooth data, or communication glitches between modules rather than a failed display panel. Many faults are inexpensive while under the 3-year warranty but can become costly afterwards, and owners report long parts lead-times.
records.solution: Apply the latest MMI software update at an Audi dealer; clear/re-pair the phone if corrupt phone data triggers it. A manual MMI reboot (press-and-hold the power/volume knob ~10 seconds) clears temporary glitches. Persistent faults may require a head-unit or module replacement.
symptoms: MMI screen freezes or goes black then reboots

records.title: Premature timing belt failure on 1.0 / 1.4 TFSI petrol engines
records.description: Owners of three-cylinder 1.0 TFSI and four-cylinder 1.4 TFSI Q2s have reported the toothed cambelt snapping well before Audi's stated 5-year / ~75,000-mile replacement interval, in several documented cases between roughly 39,000 and 49,000 km/miles, with full service history. Because these are interference engines, a snapped belt causes the valves to collide with the pistons, leading to catastrophic internal damage and frequently an entire engine replacement. Contributing factors cited by owners and forum moderators include the extra start/stop cyclical loading on the belt and frequent short journeys, plus belt tensioner/bolt loosening. Audi typically offered only partial goodwill rather than full coverage out of warranty.
records.solution: Replace the timing belt, tensioner, idlers and water pump as a kit well before the stated interval (many owners now do it at 4 years / 40k-50k miles as a precaution); if the belt has already failed, the usual outcome is a replacement engine (often a reconditioned/used unit) plus a new belt kit. Pursue Audi goodwill via the dealer/ombudsman if full service history exists.
symptoms: Engine suddenly stops/cuts out while driving
Loud snap or rattle then loss of power
Engine will not crank/start after belt fails
Bent valves / engine knocking after the event

records.title: Rear hub carrier (wheel-bearing housing) fracture recall
records.description: An early official recall covers a small batch of Q2s (around 30 vehicles, identified August 2017) in which the rear wheel-bearing housing / hub carrier could fracture due to a manufacturing defect. A cracked rear hub carrier compromises wheel location and vehicle stability, creating a loss-of-control risk. This was a limited production-defect campaign rather than a fleet-wide fault.
records.solution: Recall remedy: affected rear hub carriers are inspected and replaced at an authorised Audi dealer free of charge. Owners verify by VIN.
symptoms: Knocking or clunking from the rear axle

records.title: S tronic (DSG) dual-clutch transmission jerking, hesitation and delayed shifts
records.description: Q2s fitted with the 7-speed S tronic dual-clutch gearbox exhibit jerking when pulling away, a delay/lag in shift response, and uneven gear changes, most noticeable in stop-and-go traffic. Owner reports and reliability surveys describe these symptoms appearing relatively early (often ~20,000–40,000 km). Underlying causes range from clutch-pack wear and worn solenoids to mechatronic-unit faults and overdue fluid; in worse cases the gearbox drops into limp mode.
records.solution: Start with a transmission software/adaption update and a DSG mechatronic fluid-and-filter service at the correct interval; if symptoms persist, diagnose and replace the clutch pack or mechatronic unit as required. Address promptly to avoid limp-mode and further wear.
symptoms: Hesitation or delay before the gear engages
Rough or uneven gear changes in traffic
